caption: What if you swallowed chewing gum? Relax: the famous '7 years in your stomach' warning is a myth. Doctors who look inside stomachs with cameras say they don't find years-old wads sitting there. Gum base is a rubbery mix of resins, softeners and elastomers, and one allowed elastomer, butyl rubber, is also used in inner tubes. Your body absorbs the sugar and flavour, but it has no enzymes that break down the base, so the gum simply rides along with your food and leaves in about 40 hours. The real warning: swallowing lots of gum, often, has rarely caused blockages, mostly in young children, so spit it in the bin and keep gum away from little kids. Twist: in Denmark, scientists pulled a complete human genome out of a 5,700-year-old chewed lump of birch tar. Did YOU believe the 7-year myth? 👇
